pairs.title: A Classifier-Based Parser With Linear Run-Time Complexity
pairs.human_abstract: We present a classifier-based parser that produces constituent trees in linear time. The parser uses a basic bottom-up shiftreduce algorithm, but employs a classifier to determine parser actions instead of a grammar. This can be seen as an extension of the deterministic dependency parser of Nivre and Scholz (2004) to full constituent parsing. We show that, with an appropriate feature set used in classification, a very simple one-path greedy parser can perform at the same level of accuracy as more complex parsers. We evaluate our parser on section 23 of the WSJ section of the Penn Treebank, and obtain precision and recall of 87.54% and 87.61%, respectively.load_json_files
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper presents a simple, linear-time, classifier-based shift-reduce parser that generates both dependency and constituent structures simultaneously without an explicit grammar. The parser uses a classifier to make parsing decisions in a deterministic manner, guided by features derived from local context. Experiments demonstrate that the parser, when employing support vector machines for classification, achieves over 87% labeled constituent precision and recall on correctly POS-tagged text and runs considerably faster than state-of-the-art statistical parsers. The study highlights the significant impact of classifier choice on parser performance and proposes future work to explore additional features and classifiers.

pairs.title: A Comparison of Vector-based Representations for Semantic Composition
pairs.human_abstract: In this paper we address the problem of modeling compositional meaning for phrases and sentences using distributional methods. We experiment with several possible combinations of representation and composition, exhibiting varying degrees of sophistication. Some are shallow while others operate over syntactic structure, rely on parameter learning, or require access to very large corpora. We find that shallow approaches are as good as more computationally intensive alternatives with regards to two particular tests: (1) phrase similarity and (2) paraphrase detection. The sizes of the involved training corpora and the generated vectors are not as important as the fit between the meaning representation and compositional method.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper evaluates three distributional semantic representations—simple distributional space, neural language model embeddings, and third-order tensor models—and their effectiveness in semantic composition for natural language processing. By employing addition, multiplication, and recursive neural network methods, the study compares compositional models for their performance on phrase similarity and paraphrase detection tasks. The findings suggest that simpler models achieve comparable or superior results to more complex alternatives, highlighting the importance of selecting appropriate lexical representations and suggesting that representation and composition methods should be developed in tandem.

pairs.title: A Composite Kernel To Extract Relations Between Entities With Both Flat And Structured Features
pairs.human_abstract: This paper proposes a novel composite kernel for relation extraction. The composite kernel consists of two individual kernels: an entity kernel that allows for entity-related features and a convolution parse tree kernel that models syntactic information of relation examples. The motivation of our method is to fully utilize the nice properties of kernel methods to explore diverse knowledge for relation extraction. Our study illustrates that the composite kernel can effectively capture both flat and structured features without the need for extensive feature engineering, and can also easily scale to include more features. Evaluation on the ACE corpus shows that our method outperforms the previous best-reported methods and significantly outperforms previous two dependency tree kernels for relation extraction.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper presents a novel composite kernel for relation extraction that combines flat entity features with structured syntactic features from parse trees without extensive feature engineering. The composite kernel, integrating an entity kernel and a convolution parse tree kernel, demonstrates superior performance on the ACE corpus compared to previous methods, effectively capturing both flat and syntactic structure features. The kernel's design allows for the addition of more individual kernels to cover broader knowledge, potentially improving relation detection accuracy. The study also highlights the importance of selecting effective portions of parse trees for kernel calculations in relation extraction tasks. Future work will focus on designing a more flexible tree kernel and addressing data imbalance and sparseness issues.

pairs.title: A Corpus-Based Approach For Building Semantic Lexicons
pairs.human_abstract: Semantic knowledge can be a great asset to natural language processing systems, but it is usually hand-coded for each application. Although some semantic information is available in general-purpose knowledge bases such as WordNet and Cyc, many applications require domain-specific lexicons that represent words and categories for a particular topic. In this paper, we present a corpus-based method that can be used to build semantic lexicons for specific categories. The input to the system is a small set of seed words for a category and a representative text corpus. The output is a ranked list of words that are associated with the category. A user then reviews the top-ranked words and decides which ones should be entered in the semantic lexicon. In experiments with five categories, users typically found about 60 words per category in 10-15 minutes to build a core semantic lexicon.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This study presents a corpus-based method for semi-automatically constructing semantic lexicons. By utilizing a representative text corpus and a set of seed words for a given category, the system identifies and ranks potential category words through a bootstrapping algorithm. The method requires minimal human intervention, with a user reviewing the output list to finalize the lexicon. Experiments with various categories demonstrate the method's effectiveness, showing how it can quickly generate a core semantic lexicon with just 10-15 minutes of human review. The approach has potential for semantic knowledge acquisition and is especially adept at identifying domain-specific terms not typically considered by users. Further work is needed to refine the method and determine its applicability to different types of categories.

pairs.title: A Maximum Entropy Model For Part-Of-Speech Tagging
pairs.human_abstract: This paper presents a statistical model which trains from a corpus annotated with Part-Of- Speech tags and assigns them to previously unseen text with state-of-the-art accuracy(96.6%). The can be classified as a Entropy model and simultaneously uses many contextual "features" to predict the POS tag. Furthermore, this paper demonstrates the use of specialized features to model difficult tagging decisions, discusses the corpus consistency problems discovered during the implementation of these features, and proposes a training strategy that mitigates these problems.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper presents a Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) model for Part-Of-Speech (POS) tagging, demonstrating its effectiveness on the Wall Street Journal corpus. The model uses a rich set of contextual features and a Maximum Likelihood approach for parameter estimation, aiming to improve tagging accuracy by better utilizing context. Experiments show a state-of-the-art accuracy of 96.6% on unseen data. However, specialized features for difficult words only marginally improve performance, suggesting limitations due to inconsistencies in the training data.

pairs.title: A Monolingual Tree-based Translation Model for Sentence Simplification
pairs.human_abstract: In this paper, we consider sentence sim plification as a special form of translation with the complex sentence as the source and the simple sentence as the target. We propose a Tree-based Simplification Model (TSM), which, to our knowledge, is the first statistical simplification model covering splitting, dropping, reorderingand substitution integrally. We also de scribe an efficient method to train our model with a large-scale parallel dataset obtained from the Wikipedia and Simple Wikipedia. The evaluation shows that our model achieves better readability scores than a set of baseline systems.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper introduces a novel Monolingual Tree-based Translation Model (TSM) for Sentence Simplification that integrates operations such as splitting, dropping, reordering, and word/phrase substitution. The TSM model is designed to facilitate better reading comprehension for various reader groups, including those with reading disabilities, non-native speakers, and low-literacy readers. The model's parameters are learned from a compiled complex-simple parallel dataset (PWKP) derived from English and Simple English Wikipedia. The paper outlines a training method that employs an expectation maximization algorithm and monolingual word mapping, enhancing the efficiency of the training process. Evaluation of the TSM model demonstrates improved readability scores compared to baseline systems, indicating its effectiveness in sentence simplification tasks.

pairs.title: A New Dataset and Method for Automatically Grading ESOL Texts
pairs.human_abstract: We demonstrate how supervised discriminative machine learning techniques can be used to automate the assessment of ‘English as a Second or Other Language’ (ESOL) examination scripts. In particular, we use rank preference learning to explicitly model the grade relationships between scripts. A number of different features are extracted and ablation tests are used to investigate their contribution to overall performance. A comparison between regression and rank preference models further supports our method. Experimental results on the first publically available dataset show that our system can achieve levels of performance close to the upper bound for the task, as defined by the agreement between human examiners on the same corpus. Finally, using a set of ‘outlier’ texts, we test the validity of our model and identify cases where the model’s scores diverge from that of a human examiner.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper introduces a novel dataset and method for automatically grading English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) texts. The approach treats automated assessment as a supervised discriminative machine learning problem and specifically as a rank preference learning task. It leverages a new dataset of manually-marked ESOL examination scripts to train Support Vector Machines (SVMs) for ranking text quality without the need for retraining on new prompts. A range of linguistic features, including lexical, grammatical, and error-rate features, are automatically extracted and evaluated for their contribution to the system's performance. The results demonstrate that the new system performs close to the upper bound set by human examiners. The paper also explores the robustness of the system to 'outlier' texts, indicating areas for future improvement such as better error detection and the integration of features assessing discourse coherence.

pairs.title: A Regression Model of Adjective-Noun Compositionality in Distributional Semantics
pairs.human_abstract: In this paper we explore the computational modelling of compositionality in distributional models of semantics. In particular, we model the semantic composition of pairs of adjacent English Adjecand Nouns from the National We build a vector-based semantic space from a lemmatised version of the BNC, where the most frequent A-N lemma pairs are treated as single tokens. We then extrapolate three different models of compositionality: a simple additive model, a pointwise-multiplicative model and a Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR) model. We propose two evaluation methods for the implemented models. Our study leads to the conclusion that regression-based models of compositionality generally out-perform additive and multiplicative approaches, and also show a number of advantages that make them very promising for future research.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper presents a novel regression model for understanding adjective-noun (A-N) compositionality within distributional semantics models (DSMs). The authors focus on Partial Least Squares Regression (PLSR), a technique well-established in other fields but not previously applied to computational semantics, to address multivariate regression issues where variables exceed observations. Three models were compared: additive, multiplicative, and PLSR. The study utilized a dataset from the British National Corpus, constructing a vector space for A-N pairs. Evaluation methods relied on Euclidean distance measures and nearest neighbor comparisons. Results indicated that PLSR outperformed other models in the first evaluation setting and showed promising results overall, pointing to its effectiveness in generating neighbors for real vectors and suggesting potential applications in identifying distributional synonyms for unseen A-N pairs. The paper concludes by highlighting the importance of developing better evaluation methods and considering lexical associations in future research on compositionality in natural language.

pairs.title: A Study on Similarity and Relatedness Using Distributional and WordNet-based Approaches
pairs.human_abstract: This paper presents and compares WordNetbased and distributional similarity approaches. The strengths and weaknesses of each approach regarding similarity and relatedness tasks are discussed, and a combination is presented. Each of our methods independently provide the best results in their class on the RG and WordSim353 datasets, and a supervised combination of them yields the best published results on all datasets. Finally, we pioneer cross-lingual similarity, showing that our methods are easily adapted for a cross-lingual task with minor losses.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper investigates semantic similarity and relatedness by combining distributional methods using a large web corpus and WordNet-based approaches. The study shows that distributional similarities, especially context-window approaches, can achieve comparable results to knowledge-based methods and that combining both approaches can surpass previous performance benchmarks. The research also explores cross-lingual similarity, demonstrating that closely aligned wordnets effectively facilitate cross-lingual comparisons with minimal performance loss. The paper concludes that a supervised learner exploiting the complementarity of methods yields the best results for standard datasets.

pairs.title: A Uniform Approach to Analogies Synonyms Antonyms and Associations
pairs.human_abstract: Recognizing analogies, synonyms, anto nyms, and associations appear to be fourdistinct tasks, requiring distinct NLP al gorithms. In the past, the four tasks have been treated independently, using a widevariety of algorithms. These four seman tic classes, however, are a tiny sample of the full range of semantic phenomena, andwe cannot afford to create ad hoc algo rithms for each semantic phenomenon; weneed to seek a unified approach. We propose to subsume a broad range of phenom ena under analogies. To limit the scope of this paper, we restrict our attention to the subsumption of synonyms, antonyms, and associations. We introduce a supervised corpus-based machine learning algorithm for classifying analogous word pairs, and we show that it can solve multiple-choice SAT analogy questions, TOEFL synonymquestions, ESL synonym-antonym questions, and similar-associated-both ques tions from cognitive psychology.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper presents a novel corpus-based approach to natural language processing (NLP) that uniformly addresses the recognition of analogies, synonyms, antonyms, and associations. The authors propose that these semantic relationships can all be understood as analogies and demonstrate the application of a standard supervised machine learning algorithm to classify word pairs across these four semantic categories. The algorithm, PairClass, uses feature vectors generated from pattern frequencies in a large corpus and a support vector machine (SVM) to classify the relationships. Experiments using SAT analogy questions, TOEFL synonym questions, ESL practice questions, and cognitive psychology word pair sets show that PairClass is competitive with specialized algorithms, achieving accuracy levels that are on par or better than existing systems. The research suggests that a uniform approach to semantic phenomena is feasible and can be advantageous compared to developing specialized algorithms for each task.

pairs.title: An Algorithm For Generating Quantifier Scopings
pairs.human_abstract: The syntactic structure of a sentence often manifests quite clearly the predicate-argument structure and relations of grammatical subordination. But scope dependencies are not so transparent. As a result, many systems for representing the semantics of sentences have ignored scoping or generated scopings with mechanisms that have often been inexplicit as to the range of scopings they choose among or profligate in the scopings they allow. This paper presents, along with proofs of some of its important properties, an algorithm that generates scoped semantic forms from unscoped expressions encoding predicate-argument structure. The algorithm is not profligate as are those based on permutation of quantifiers, and it can provide a solid foundation for computational solutions where completeness is sacrificed for efficiency and heuristic efficacy.

The authors discuss the inadequacies of previous computational efforts which often lacked explicitness in scoping mechanisms and were profligate in the scope readings they allowed. In contrast, their algorithm produces scoped semantic forms from unscoped expressions and is demonstrated to be more selective and efficient. pairs.title: Chinese Syntactic Reordering for Statistical Machine Translation
pairs.human_abstract: Syntactic reordering approaches are an effective method for handling word-order differences between source and target lan guages in statistical machine translation(SMT) systems. This paper introduces a reordering approach for translation from Chinese to English. We describe a set of syntac tic reordering rules that exploit systematic differences between Chinese and English word order. The resulting system is used as a preprocessor for both training and test sentences, transforming Chinese sentences to be much closer to English in terms of their word order. We evaluated the reordering approach within the MOSES phrase-based SMT system (Koehn et al, 2007). The reordering approach improved the BLEU score for the MOSES system from 28.52 to 30.86 on the NIST 2006 evaluation data. Wealso conducted a series of experiments to an alyze the accuracy and impact of different types of reordering rules.

pairs.title: CogNIAC: High Precision Coreference With Limited Knowledge And Linguistic Resources
pairs.human_abstract: This paper presents a high precision pronoun resolution system that is capable of greater than 90% precision with 60% and better recall for some pronouns. It is suggested that the system is resolving a sub-set of anaphors that do not require general world knowledge or sophisticated linguistic processing for successful resolution. The system does this by being very sensitive to ambiguity, and only resolving pronouns when very high confidence rules have been satisfied. The system is capable of 'noticing' ambiguity because it requires that there be a unique antecedent within a salience ranking, and the salience rankings are not total orders, i.e. two or more antecedents can be equally salient. Given the nature of the systems rules, it is very likely that they are largely domain independent and that they reflect processing strategies used by humans for general language comprehension. The system has been evaluated in two distinct experiments which support the overall validity of the approach.

CogNIAC differentiates itself from similar algorithms by avoiding resolution in ambiguous contexts, thereby achieving high precision. pairs.human_abstract: Most work in statistical parsing has focused on a single corpus: the Wall Street Journal portion of the Penn Treebank. While this has allowed for quantitative comparison of parsing techniques, it has left open the question of how other types of text might affect parser performance, and how portable parsing models are across corpora. We examine these questions by comparing results for the Brown and WSJ corpora, and also consider which parts of the parser's probability model are particularly tuned to the corpus on which it was trained. This leads us to a technique for pruning parameters to reduce the size of the parsing model.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper investigates the impact of corpus variation on the performance of statistical natural language parsers. It addresses how well a parsing model trained on one corpus can adapt to another and evaluates the significance of lexical dependency features in parsing models. Results show that matched training data is more beneficial than unmatched, larger data sets. Surprisingly, over a third of the model's parameters, specifically lexical bigrams, can be eliminated with minimal performance impact. This finding suggests that lighter, more memory-efficient parsers can be developed without significant loss in accuracy. Further research is suggested to explore the applicability of complex features across different corpora.

pairs.title: Edge-Based Best-First Chart Parsing
pairs.human_abstract: Best-first probabilistic chart parsing attempts to parse efficiently by working on edges that are judged "best" by some probabilistic figure of merit (FOM). Recent work has used probabilistic context-free grammars (PCFGs) to assign probabilities to constituents, and to use these probabilities as the starting point for the FOM. This paper extends this approach to using a probabilistic FOM to judge edges (incomplete constituents), thereby giving a much finergrained control over parsing effort. We show how this can be accomplished in a particularly simple way using the common idea of binarizing the PCFG. The results obtained are about a facof twenty improvement over the best results — that is, our parser achieves equivalent results using one twentieth the number of edges. Furthermore we show that this improvement is obtained with parsing precision and recall levels superior to those achieved by exhaustive parsing.

A significant innovation is the use of the FOM to rank all edges, including incomplete ones, which dramatically reduces the number of edges required for parsing. The paper describes binarization techniques, experimental setups using the Penn Wall Street Journal text, and compares the results to previous research. The findings demonstrate that the proposed edge-based method significantly outperforms existing approaches in terms of the number of edges processed. The authors suggest that their FOM-based parser likely concentrates on plausible edges given their context, leading to more accurate parses. They conclude by highlighting the potential for applying these techniques to more complex probabilistic models and advocate for further research in this area.

pairs.title: Evaluating The Accuracy Of An Unlexicalized Statistical Parser On The PARC DepBank
pairs.human_abstract: We evaluate the accuracy of an unlexicalized statistical parser, trained on 4K treebanked sentences from balanced data and tested on the PARC DepBank. The comparison of systems using DepBank is not straightforward, so we extend and validate DepBank and highlight a number of representation and scoring issues for relational evaluation schemes.

pairs.title: Extracting Parallel Sub-Sentential Fragments From Non-Parallel Corpora
pairs.human_abstract: We present a novel method for extracting parallel sub-sentential fragments from comparable, non-parallel bilingual corpora. By analyzing potentially similar sentence pairs using a signal processinginspired approach, we detect which segments of the source sentence are translated into segments in the target sentence, and which are not. This method enables us to extract useful machine translation training data even from very non-parallel corpora, which contain no parallel sentence pairs. We evaluate the quality of the extracted data by showing that it improves the performance of a state-of-the-art statistical machine translation system.

Recognizing the limitations of existing sentence-level parallel data extraction methods, the authors focus on sub-sentential fragments that are more prevalent in non-parallel texts. They present an innovative algorithm and a probabilistic lexicon based on the Log-Likelihood Ratio statistic to enhance the precision of extraction. Experiments demonstrate the method's effectiveness in improving SMT, particularly when full parallel sentences are scarce.

pairs.title: Finite-State Transducers In Language And Speech Processing
pairs.human_abstract: Finite-state machines have been used in various domains of natural language processing. We consider here the use of a type of transducer that supports very efficient programs: sequential transducers. We recall classical theorems and give new ones characterizing sequential string-tostring transducers. Transducers that output weights also play an important role in language and speech processing. We give a specific study of string-to-weight transducers, including algorithms for determinizing and minimizing these transducers very efficiently, and characterizations of the transducers admitting determinization and the corresponding algorithms. Some applications of these algorithms in speech recognition are described and illustrated.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study of finite-state transducers (FSTs) in language and speech processing. Sequential transducers are shown to be highly efficient for string-to-string and string-to-weight transformations, with new characterizations and algorithms for determinizing and minimizing these transducers. The paper also explores the practical applications of these algorithms in speech recognition, demonstrating the reduction of complexity and improvement of efficiency in recognizing and processing large linguistic datasets. Theoretical foundations are complemented with algorithmic implementations and the potential for reshaping methods in computational linguistics and speech processing is discussed.

pairs.title: Forest Rescoring: Faster Decoding with Integrated Language Models
pairs.human_abstract: Efficient decoding has been a fundamental problem in machine translation, especially with an integrated language model which is essential for achieving good translation quality. We develop faster approaches for problem based on parsing algorithms and demonstrate their effectiveness on both phrase-based and syntax-based MT systems. In both cases, our methods achieve significant speed improvements, often by more than a factor of ten, over the conventional beam-search method at the same levels of search error and translation accuracy.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper introduces "forest rescoring," an efficient method for integrating language models into the decoding process of statistical machine translation. This approach offers an order of magnitude faster performance than full-integration methods, with comparable accuracy and search error levels as measured by BLEU. Experiments on large-scale English-to-Chinese translation tasks demonstrate substantial speed improvements, often exceeding a factor of ten.

pairs.title: Fully Unsupervised Discovery of Concept-Specific Relationships by Web Mining
pairs.human_abstract: We present a web mining method for discovering and enhancing relationships in which a specified concept (word class) participates. We discover a whole range of relationships focused on the given concept, rather than generic known relationships as in most previous work. Our method is based on clustering patterns that contain concept words and other words related to them. We evaluate the method on three different rich concepts and find that in each case the method generates a broad variety of relationships with good precision.

The method is suitable for web mining despite search engine query limitations. The approach was tested on concepts like countries, fish species, and constellations, showing that it can effectively produce a diverse collection of relations. The results demonstrate the potential of the method for studying and researching specific concepts or fields.

pairs.title: Generating Natural Language Summaries From Multiple On-Line Sources
pairs.human_abstract: We present a methodology for summarization of news about current events in the form of briefings that include appropriate background (historical) information. The system that we developed, SUMMONS, uses the output of systems developed for the DARPA Message Understanding Conferences to generate summaries of multiple documents on the same or related events, presenting similarities and differences, contradictions, and generalizations among sources of information. We describe the various components of the system, showing how information from multiple articles is combined, organized into a paragraph, and finally, realized as English sentences. A feature of our work is the extraction of descriptions of entities such as people and places for reuse to enhance a briefing.

SUMMONS stands out by synthesizing similarities, differences, and contradictions across various reports, and by providing historical context for the events described. The system incorporates outputs from DARPA Message Understanding Conferences, creating summaries that are not only informative but also fluent and coherent in English. A major challenge addressed is the overwhelming volume of information available on the Internet, which makes it difficult for users to manually process all relevant documents on a topic. SUMMONS aims to alleviate this by providing search, selection, and summarization services. The paper details the components of SUMMONS, the methodology behind it, and the use of extracted entity descriptions to enhance briefings. The system focuses on the domain of news on terrorism and has the potential to be adapted to other domains with further research.

pairs.human_abstract: Machine learning approaches to coreference resolution are typically supervised, and require expensive labeled data. On MUC and ACE datasets, our model outperforms Haghigi and Klein’s one using only a fraction of the training data, and often matches or exceeds the accuracy of state-of-the-art supervised models.

pairs.human_abstract: Morphology induction is a subproblem of important tasks like automatic learning of machine-readable dictionaries and grammar induction. Previous morphology induction approaches have relied solely on statistics of hypothesized stems and affixes to choose which affixes to consider legitimate. We introduce a semantic-based algorithm for learning morphology which only proposes affixes when the stem and stem-plusaffix are sufficiently similar semantically. pairs.title: Learning Subjective Language
pairs.human_abstract: Subjectivity in natural language refers to aspects of language used to express opinions, evaluations, and speculations. There are numerous natural language processing applications for which subjectivity analysis is relevant, including information extraction and text categorization. The goal of this work is learning subjective language from corpora. Clues of subjectivity are generated and tested, including low-frequency words, collocations, and adjectives and verbs identified using distributional similarity. The features are also examined working together in concert. The features, generated from different data sets using different procedures, exhibit consistency in performance in that they all do better and worse on the same data sets. In addition, this article shows that the density of subjectivity clues in the surrounding context strongly affects how likely it is that a word is subjective, and it provides the results of an annotation study assessing the subjectivity of sentences with high-density features. Finally, the clues are used to perform opinion piece recognition (a type of text categorization and genre detection) to demonstrate the utility of the knowledge acquired in this article.

pairs.title: Linguistic Regularities in Continuous Space Word Representations
pairs.human_abstract: Continuous space language models have recently demonstrated outstanding results across a variety of tasks. In this paper, we examine the vector-space word representations that are implicitly learned by the input-layer weights. We find that these representations are surprisingly good at capturing syntactic and semantic regularities in language, and that each relationship is characterized by a relation-specific vector offset. This allows vector-oriented reasoning based on the offsets between words. For example, the male/female relationship is automatically learned, and with the induced vector representations, “King - Man + Woman” results in a vector very close to “Queen.” We demonstrate that the word vectors capture syntactic regularities by means of syntactic analogy questions (provided with this paper), and are able to correctly answer almost 40% of the questions. We demonstrate that the word vectors capture semantic regularities by using the vector offset method to answer SemEval-2012 Task 2 questions. Remarkably, this method outperforms the best previous systems.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper explores the syntactic and semantic regularities captured by continuous space word representations learned through a recurrent neural network language model (RNNLM). The authors propose a vector offset method based on cosine distance that effectively identifies relationships between words as constant vector offsets. They demonstrate that RNNLM-generated word vectors exhibit significant syntactic regularity and semantic information, surpassing traditional n-gram models and other existing approaches like Latent Semantic Analysis (LSA) and Hierarchical Log-Bilinear (HLBL) models. The paper introduces a new dataset for measuring syntactic analogy performance, achieving nearly 40% accuracy, as well as evaluates semantic generalization using the SemEval 2012 task, where it outperforms the previous state-of-the-art. The findings suggest that even unsupervised training on large text corpora can result in meaningful word representations that capture linguistic regularities.

pairs.title: Local Phrase Reordering Models For Statistical Machine Translation
pairs.human_abstract: We describe stochastic models of localphrase movement that can be incorporated into a Statistical Machine Translation (SMT) system. These models pro vide properly formulated, non-deficient, probability distributions over reorderedphrase sequences. They are implemented by Weighted Finite State Trans ducers. We describe EM-style parameter re-estimation procedures based on phrase alignment under the complete translationmodel incorporating reordering. Our ex periments show that the reordering modelyields substantial improvements in trans lation performance on Arabic-to-English and Chinese-to-English MT tasks. We also show that the procedure scales as the bitext size is increased.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper presents statistical machine translation (SMT) models for local phrase reordering, crucial for capturing natural language differences between source and target languages. The authors develop models that can be embedded in a generative phrase-based translation framework, allowing for computationally feasible Maximum A Posteriori decoding and parameter re-estimation using Expectation Maximization over large bitext collections. These models are implemented as Weighted Finite State Transducers (WFSTs) and are shown to improve alignment and translation performance for Arabic-English and Chinese-English tasks. The paper also discusses the integration of these models into larger SMT systems, demonstrating significant improvements in translation quality and confirming the effectiveness of the reordering models when combined with discriminative training techniques.

pairs.title: Machine Learning For Coreference Resolution: From Local Classification To Global Ranking
pairs.human_abstract: In this paper, we view coreference resolution as a problem of ranking candidate partitions generated by different coreference systems. We propose a set of partition-based features to learn a ranking model for distinguishing good and bad partitions. Our approach compares favorably to two state-of-the-art coreference systems when evaluated on three standard coreference data sets.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper proposes a machine learning approach to coreference resolution that improves robustness by generating multiple candidate NP partitions and employing a ranking model to select the best one. The method minimizes ad-hoc design decisions and optimizes for clustering-level accuracy. Experiments show favorable results compared to state-of-the-art systems on standard data sets.

pairs.title: Machine Translation by Triangulation: Making Effective Use of Multi-Parallel Corpora
pairs.human_abstract: Current phrase-based SMT systems perform poorly when using small training sets. This is a consequence of unreliable translation estimates and low coverage over source and target phrases. This paper presents a method which alleviates this problem by exploiting multiple translations of the same source Central to our approach is triangulathe process of translating from a source to a target language via an intermediate third language. This allows the use of a much wider range of parallel corpora for training, and can be combined with a standard phrase-table using conventional smoothing methods. Experimental results demonstrate BLEU improvements for triangulated models over a standard phrase-based system.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper introduces a novel triangulation method for statistical machine translation (SMT) that leverages multi-parallel corpora to improve translation quality, especially when training on small datasets. The triangulation method involves translating a phrase from the source to the target language via one or multiple intermediate languages, thus enhancing the robustness of phrase translation estimates and addressing data sparseness by utilizing additional multi-parallel data. Experiments demonstrate significant performance gains on small datasets and improvements on larger datasets when combined with standard phrase-tables. The method particularly benefits from using intermediate languages closely related to the source or target language, and shows promise for translating between low-density language pairs.

pairs.title: Meaningful Clustering Of Senses Helps Boost Word Sense Disambiguation Performance
pairs.human_abstract: Fine-grained sense distinctions are one of the major obstacles to successful Word Sense Disambiguation. In this paper, we present a method for reducing the granularity of the WordNet sense inventory based on the mapping to a manually crafted dictionary encoding sense hierarchies, namely the Oxford Dictionary of English. We assess the quality of the mapping and the induced clustering, and evaluate the performance of coarse WSD systems in the Senseval-3 English all-words task.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper investigates the impact of clustering WordNet senses into coarser-grained categories to enhance Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) performance. It introduces a method for mapping WordNet senses to Oxford Dictionary of English entries, producing a reduced and more manageable sense inventory. Evaluation against a manually annotated gold standard shows that using coarse-grained sense inventories significantly improves the accuracy of WSD systems. The paper underscores the potential of coarse-grained sense distinctions in various language-aware applications.

pairs.title: Minimum Error Rate Training In Statistical Machine Translation
pairs.human_abstract: Often, the training procedure for statistical machine translation models is based on maximum likelihood or related criteria. A general problem of this approach is that there is only a loose relation to the final translation quality on unseen text. In this paper, we analyze various training criteria which directly optimize translation quality. These training criteria make use of recently proposed automatic evaluation metrics. We describe a new algorithm for efficient training an unsmoothed error count. We show that significantly better results can often be obtained if the final evaluation criterion is taken directly into account as part of the training procedure.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper investigates methods for optimizing statistical machine translation (SMT) model parameters with respect to automatic evaluation criteria such as word error rate and BLEU. It challenges the mismatch between the basic assumptions of statistical approaches and the desired evaluation criteria, proposing training models that directly optimize for translation quality. The paper introduces new training algorithms, including an efficient line optimization algorithm for an unsmoothed error count, and evaluates these methods in machine translation experiments. Results indicate that optimizing for specific error rates during training can significantly improve performance on corresponding evaluation metrics, suggesting a direct correlation with improved translation quality.

pairs.title: Modeling Local Coherence: An Entity-Based Approach
pairs.human_abstract: This article proposes a novel framework for representing and measuring local coherence. Central to this approach is the entity-grid representation of discourse, which captures patterns of entity distribution in a text. The algorithm introduced in the article automatically abstracts a text into a set of entity transition sequences and records distributional, syntactic, and referential information about discourse entities. We re-conceptualize coherence assessment as a learning task and show that our entity-based representation is well-suited for ranking-based generation and text classification tasks. Using the proposed representation, we achieve good performance on text ordering, summary coherence evaluation, and readability assessment.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper introduces an entity-grid framework to quantify and assess local text coherence by tracking entity distributions and transitions across sentences. The novel approach abstracts texts into entity transition sequences, incorporating distributional, syntactic, and referential properties of discourse entities. Coherence assessment is treated as a learning task, and the entity-based representation proves effective in ranking coherent texts and classifying readability levels. The framework outperforms state-of-the-art models in text ordering, summarization coherence rating, and readability assessment tasks, demonstrating its adaptability across various domains and genres. The research also explores the parameters influencing grid construction, such as coreference, syntactic information, and entity salience, and suggests future directions for integrating lexico-semantic knowledge and global discourse structure into the model.

pairs.title: NLTK: The Natural Language Toolkit
pairs.human_abstract: NLTK, the Natural Language Toolkit, is a suite of open source program modules, tutorials and problem sets, providing ready-to-use computational linguistics courseware. NLTK covers symbolic and statistical natural language processing, and is interfaced to annotated corpora. Students augment and replace existing components, learn structured programming by example, and manipulate sophisticated models from the outset.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: The paper introduces the Natural Language Toolkit (NLTK), an open-source Python package developed for teaching computational linguistics. NLTK simplifies practical programming in the field by providing a uniform framework for assignments, projects, and demonstrations. With extensive documentation and easy-to-use modules, it allows students to focus on NLP system building without worrying about underlying infrastructure.

pairs.title: Named Entity Recognition Using An HMM-Based Chunk Tagger
pairs.human_abstract: This paper proposes a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) and an HMM-based chunk tagger, from which a named entity (NE) recognition (NER) system is built to recognize and classify names, times and numerical quantities. Through the HMM, our system is able to apply and integrate four types of internal and external evidences: 1) simple deterministic internal feature of the words, such as capitalization and digitalization; 2) internal semantic feature of important triggers; 3) internal gazetteer feature; 4) external macro context feature. In this way, the NER problem can be resolved effectively. Evaluation of our system on MUC-6 and MUC-7 English NE tasks achieves F-measures of 96.6% and 94.1% respectively. It shows that the performance is significantly better than reported by any other machine-learning system. Moreover, the performance is even consistently better than those based on handcrafted rules.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper presents a Hidden Markov Model (HMM)-based chunk tagger for Named Entity Recognition (NER), which classifies words into predefined categories. The paper addresses the limitations of rule-based systems, emphasizing the advantages of machine-learning approaches in terms of adaptability and maintenance costs. The proposed HMM chunk tagger is demonstrated to effectively use both internal and external evidences, such as word capitalization, semantic triggers, and contextual information, to improve NER accuracy. Experimental results indicate that the system outperforms previously published machine-learning and rule-based systems in English NER tasks. The paper also discusses the impact of training data size on performance and the contribution of different sub-features to the system's effectiveness. The authors suggest that while the system performs near human-level accuracy, there is still potential for further improvement.

pairs.title: Named Entity Recognition With Character-Level Models
pairs.human_abstract: We discuss two named-entity recognition models which use characters and character -grams either exclusively or as an important part of their data representation. The first model is a character-level HMM with minimal context information, and the second model is a maximum-entropy conditional markov model with substantially richer context features. Our best model achieves an overall F of 86.07% on the English test data (92.31% on the development data). This number represents a 25% error reduction over the same model without word-internal (substring) features.
pairs.gpt4_abstract: This paper presents a study on the effectiveness of character-level models for Named Entity Recognition (NER) tasks, as opposed to traditional word-level models. It introduces a character-level Hidden Markov Model (HMM) and a sequence-free maximum-entropy (maxent) classifier employing character n-gram substring features. Additionally, a Conditional Markov Model (CMM) is proposed, integrating state sequence features for improved classification interaction. The results demonstrate significant error reduction when using character-based models and feature engineering in a maxent framework, yielding superior performance in NER tasks.
